title: Cancer cachexia
bottleneck: Cancer cachexia, the progressive loss of skeletal muscle and fat driven by tumor-induced inflammation and metabolic derangement, affects up to 80% of patients with advanced pancreatic, gastric, and lung cancers. It cannot be reversed by nutrition alone and directly causes an estimated 20 to 30% of cancer deaths through wasting, weakness, and treatment intolerance.
why_it_blocks: Cachexia robs patients of the strength to tolerate therapy, degrades quality of life, and kills independently of tumor burden, yet it is rarely the primary endpoint of drug development.
current_state: No approved therapy reverses cachexia; investigational agents targeting inflammatory cytokines, ghrelin signaling, and muscle-wasting pathways have shown modest or inconsistent results. It remains one of oncology's most neglected unsolved problems. Multidisciplinary approaches combining nutrition, exercise, and anti-inflammatory agents show the most promise, though the evidence base remains preliminary.
